cost_model.qualification: This exact two-round NTLM fixture, fresh replacement transports and one prepared binding failure each eight cycles; not a universal Kerberos or busy-borrowed-connection formula.
cost_model.consequence: Per-candidate catch-up grows linearly with this replacement history; aggregate catch-up is quadratic. Application file traffic does not advance this original-key cursor.
cost_model.round_trip_boundary: The ECHO count is not an extra-RTT count; available credits and the existing bounded pipelining determine batch sizes.

resource_evidence: After every cycle the SDK retains two live channels, one logical Session, two channel keys, no pending binding, one owned channel reference and at most 16 sparse bootstrap exclusions.
All 1126 retired connections per profile are collectible; open descriptors return to 88/88 for the first two profiles and 91/91 for the other six. Live thread differences are between -2 and +3.

Heap snapshots include JVM and test probe state and are taken after explicit GC; this is not an allocation profile or a proof of arbitrary-history memory bounds. The test JVM limit is 384 MiB and its reported processor count is two.
latency_boundary: Binding times exclude the deliberately held I/O gate. Jacoco-instrumented, shared-host, loopback fixture measurements are descriptive; no controlled comparative throughput or service-level claim.
audit_boundary: The churn probe checks actual original-key bytes, never-repeated original-key request MIDs and distinct operational channel-key bytes. It does not independently verify every packet MAC. Separate JCE wire audits are recorded in validation-peer-reauthentication-denial.json.
provenance: Existing committed workload and fixture used unchanged with the already supported --churn-cycles option. No new Java, dependency or donor import.
not_established: Arbitrary replacement-history latency, a constant catch-up packet bound, transfer scaling or sustained cancellation/transport-queue allocation pressure.
